title: Hardware Interface
description: Review of the firmware's view of the hardware: pin and peripheral configuration against the schematic, clocks, drivers, errata, sensing, outputs and display.

items.text: Pin assignments and alternate functions match the current schematic revision
items.hint: Compare the pinmux (or the config tool's file) with the schematic net names, pin by pin. Revisions drift.

items.text: Unused pins are set to a defined state
items.hint: Analog or output-low per the datasheet's advice. Floating inputs draw current and pick up noise.

items.text: Outputs that drive actuators are safe from reset until firmware sets them
items.hint: Check the pin's reset state and any external pull. A relay or heater must not pulse during boot.

items.text: Pull-ups, pull-downs and drive strength match what the circuit expects
items.hint: Internal pulls duplicated or missing against the schematic; drive strength too high for EMI.

items.text: Peripheral instances and DMA channels are allocated without conflicts
items.hint: Keep a table of which peripheral, DMA stream and interrupt each driver owns.

items.text: The pin and peripheral table is generated or checked by a tool, not copied by hand
items.hint: E.g. the vendor's config tool output, or a script that cross-checks the netlist.

items.text: The clock tree is configured as designed, and the derived frequencies are verified
items.hint: Measure the system clock on an MCO pin or by timing a known loop on real hardware.

items.text: Peripheral clocks give baud rates and sample rates within tolerance
items.hint: UART baud error under about 2%. Check every rate at every system clock setting used.

items.text: Crystal or oscillator startup failure is detected and handled
items.hint: Use the clock security system or a startup timeout, and fall back to the internal oscillator.

items.text: Timer resolution and wrap-around are handled for every timebase
items.hint: A 32-bit millisecond tick wraps after 49.7 days. Compare with subtraction, not absolute values.

items.text: RTC accuracy and drift correction meet the timekeeping requirement
items.hint: Calibrate the 32.768 kHz crystal or resync from the network.

items.text: The silicon errata for the exact part and revision are reviewed, and workarounds are in place
items.hint: Note the die revision on the prototype boards. Errata differ between revisions.

items.text: Every driver checks return codes and has timeouts on hardware waits
items.hint: No unbounded while (!flag) loops. A stuck I2C bus must not hang the system.

items.text: I2C bus recovery is implemented for a slave holding SDA low
items.hint: Clock out nine pulses and send a STOP, then reinitialize the peripheral.

items.text: Cache, DMA and memory barriers are handled where the core has caches
items.hint: Clean or invalidate around DMA buffers, or place them in non-cacheable memory.

items.text: External devices are initialized in the order their datasheets require
items.hint: Power sequencing, reset-release delays and the first register writes.

items.text: Device IDs or WHO_AM_I registers are read at startup to detect missing or wrong parts
items.hint: Makes second-source parts and assembly errors visible in production test.

items.text: ADC sampling time and reference suit each source impedance
items.hint: High-impedance sources need longer sample times or a buffer.

items.text: Filtering and averaging are designed for the noise and the response time required
items.hint: Document the filter's cutoff or time constant and its effect on latency.

items.text: Calibration constants are stored, versioned and range-checked on load
items.hint: A blank or corrupt calibration must be detected and flagged, not used.

items.text: Open, short and out-of-range sensor readings are detected
items.hint: Report a sensor fault instead of acting on an impossible value.

items.text: Fixed-point scaling and overflow are analyzed, or floating point is used deliberately
items.hint: Check the worst-case intermediate values. Note whether the FPU is used in interrupts.

items.text: Self-heating and nearby heat sources are compensated where they affect a measurement
items.hint: E.g. a temperature sensor near the MCU or the display backlight.

items.text: Outputs go to a safe state on any fault, reset or watchdog timeout
items.hint: Define the safe state per output. Verify it by forcing each fault on the bench.

items.text: Minimum on and off times, interlocks and rate limits protect the load
items.hint: E.g. compressor short-cycle protection, H-bridge dead time, relay contact wear.

items.text: Output state is read back or confirmed where the hardware allows
items.hint: Detect a welded relay or an open load.

items.text: Control loops are tuned, with gains and limits documented
items.hint: Anti-windup, output clamps, and behavior when the feedback sensor fails.

items.text: Overcurrent and stall protection respond within the hardware's limits
items.hint: Firmware protection needs a known worst-case response time, or hardware protection behind it.

items.text: Display initialization follows the panel's power and reset sequence
items.hint: VDDIO, VDD, reset release, init commands, then the backlight.

items.text: Touch input is debounced and filtered against false presses
items.hint: Includes water, ESD and a hand resting on the panel.

items.text: The touch controller and display recover after ESD or a glitch without a full reset
items.hint: Detect a stuck controller (no interrupts, bad ID) and reinitialize it.

items.text: Frame buffer and graphics memory fit the RAM budget, including fonts and images
items.hint: Count partial-refresh buffers and double buffering.

items.text: Text, units and formats can be localized if the product needs it
items.hint: Units (°C or °F), date and time formats, character sets.
